speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your hematuria and right flank pain, can you describe the severity of the pain and whether it radiates to your groin?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain radiate to your groin, and have you experienced any nausea or vomiting along with these symptoms? Additionally, do you have a personal or family history of kidney stones?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any fever, chills, or dysuria (painful urination) with these symptoms? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis Appearance: Reddish; WBC: 10-20 /HPF; RBC: Too numerous to count; Nitrites: Negative; Leukocyte_Esterase: Positive

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of recurrent UTIs and positive leukocyte esterase, I am concerned about a kidney infection or stone. Do you currently have a fever, chills, or pain when urinating? REQUEST TEST: CT_Kidney_Ureter_Bladder

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT scan is normal, we can rule out kidney stones or structural abnormalities. Given your history of recurrent UTIs and the positive leukocyte esterase, do you currently have any fever, chills, or burning sensation during urination?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT is normal and you lack systemic signs of infection, could this hematuria be related to a recent vigorous exercise or is it persistent at rest? I need to rule out exercise-induced hematuria or a glomerular source.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or any recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you deny fever, dysuria, or recent exercise, and the CT scan is normal, I need to assess for glomerular disease. Have you noticed any swelling in your legs or around your eyes, or have you experienced a recent upper respiratory infection? REQUEST TEST: Serum_Creatinine

speaker: Doctor
text: Your creatinine is normal, which is reassuring. Have you noticed any swelling in your legs or around your eyes, or a recent upper respiratory infection? REQUEST TEST: Urine_Microscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging, renal function, and urine microscopy, we must consider non-glomerular causes like early malignancy or vascular issues. Do you have any history of exposure to industrial chemicals or analgesic abuse, and have you noticed any weight loss or night sweats? REQUEST TEST: Cystoscopy
